start_command: cd backend && export DATABASE_PATH=./eval-f.db JWT_SECRET=eval-secret-at-least-32-bytes-long-0123456789 PROVIDER_TIMEZONE=UTC APP_ENV=dev && rm -f eval-f.db && uv run alembic upgrade head && uv run uvicorn telemed.api.app:create_app --factory --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 > ../eval-f-server.log 2>&1
start_note: Backend :8000 only (API-only group, no frontend). DATABASE_PATH is relative to backend/, so sqlite3 inspection targets backend/eval-f.db. JWT_SECRET must be exported (min 32 bytes). Insert an admin via sqlite3 (argon2 hash via uv run python, same technique as groups C/D/E) and log in via POST /api/auth/login. Create doctors via POST /api/admin/doctors (generates 14 days of slots): doctor A fee 500.00, doctor B fee 300.00. Register >= 21 patients via POST /api/auth/register and log in each (20 for the race, 1 spare). Slot states for F056/F057 (BOOKED, BLOCKED, past, now+15d) are arranged by sqlite3 UPDATE on slots.status/start_time, or BLOCKED via PUT /api/doctors/me/slots/{id}/block. Doctor deactivation via the admin deactivate route if mounted, else sqlite3 UPDATE users SET active=0. The 20-way race is fired from a script (e.g. python httpx/asyncio.gather or xargs -P20 curl) with barrier-style simultaneous start; DB state is verified with sqlite3 afterwards. The payment stub is in-process and not observable over HTTP: F059 call-count is verified by running the repo's pytest integration test (backend/tests/integration/test_booking.py) which overrides PaymentService with a spy; the HTTP-visible part (fee string) is checked live.

api_checks.note: setup/regression: GET /health -> 200; admin login; onboard doctors A (fee 500.00) and B (fee 300.00) (201, slots_created > 0); register and log in 21 patients. Failure blocks the group.

as patient P1, pick an AVAILABLE slot S1 of doctor A within (now, now+14d) (GET /api/doctors/{A}/slots). Snapshot appointments count and appointment_events count via sqlite3, then POST {"slot_id": S1}.

expect_body_fields.start_time: ISO datetime equal to the slot's start_time

api_checks.note: database effects via sqlite3 after F-API-1a: slots.status for S1 is BOOKED; exactly one new appointments row with slot_id=S1, patient=P1, status BOOKED; exactly one appointment_events row for that appointment with type BOOKED (and no other event rows). Slot is no longer returned by GET /api/doctors/{A}/slots.
re-booking the same slot S1 by another patient P2 -> 409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE; appointment and event counts unchanged.
nonexistent slot_id 999999 as patient -> 404 NOT_FOUND; no rows created.
body missing slot_id, and slot_id "abc" -> 422 VALIDATION_ERROR with errors[].field slot_id; no rows created.

pick a fresh AVAILABLE slot S2 of doctor A. Fire 20 simultaneous POST /api/appointments {slot_id:S2}, each with a distinct patient token (P1..P20), released together. Tally status codes: exactly one 201, exactly nineteen 409 (code SLOT_UNAVAILABLE), zero 503, zero 5xx, zero connection errors. Verify via sqlite3: exactly one appointments row for S2, exactly one BOOKED event for it, slot S2 BOOKED. Repeat the burst once on another slot S3 to rule out luck.
BOOKED slot: book the already-booked S1 as P3 -> 409. Snapshot appointments count before/after: unchanged.
BLOCKED slot: doctor A PUT block on slot S4, then P3 books S4 -> 409; slot still BLOCKED; no appointment row.
past slot: sqlite3 set an AVAILABLE slot S5's start_time/end_time to 1h in the past (format matching existing rows); book -> 409; slot stays AVAILABLE; no appointment.
beyond-window slot: sqlite3 set an AVAILABLE slot S6 start_time to now+15d; book -> 409; slot stays AVAILABLE; no appointment. Boundary sanity: a slot at now+13d23h books successfully (201).

deactivate doctor B (no live appointments), take one of B's AVAILABLE future slot ids S7 (read before deactivation), POST as patient P3 -> 409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE (not 404, not 201). Verify via sqlite3 that S7 is still AVAILABLE and no appointment was created.
doctor A token POSTs with a valid AVAILABLE slot id -> 403; admin token -> 403 (admin never books for a patient). Slot stays AVAILABLE; no rows created.
no Authorization header -> 401; garbage bearer token -> 401. Slot unchanged.
access-rule order (api-contracts 0.2): doctor token with nonexistent slot_id or invalid body -> 403 (not 404/422); no token with invalid body -> 401.

live check: book an AVAILABLE slot of doctor A (fee 500.00) as a patient; response fee is the JSON string "500.00" (matches ^\d+\.\d{2}$, not a number) and equals the doctor's profile fee; appointments row stores the fee snapshot.

payment stub call count: run the repo test that overrides PaymentService with a spy (cd backend && uv run pytest tests/integration/test_booking.py -k payment) and confirm it asserts charge called exactly once on success and zero times on a 409. Also confirm failed bookings (F-API-3a) do not invoke the stub (spy count 0).
api_checks.expect_status: pytest pass; spy.charge.call_count == 1 on success, 0 on conflict

content_rules: E3-S2 AC1/AC2: slot claim is a single conditional UPDATE (slots SET status='BOOKED' WHERE slot_id=? AND status='AVAILABLE' AND start_time window AND doctor active) in slots_repo.py, checking rowcount == 1; no read-then-write availability check in booking_service
E3-S2 AC1/AC2: slot UPDATE, appointment INSERT and BOOKED event INSERT occur inside one transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE per API-21); failure of any step rolls back all three
E3-S2 AC2: rowcount 0 raises SlotUnavailableException mapped to 409 code SLOT_UNAVAILABLE; SQLite lock contention does not surface as 503 (busy timeout / immediate transaction handled)
E3-S2 AC3: window predicate in SQL is now < start_time < now + 14 days, so BOOKED, BLOCKED, past and beyond-window slots all fail the single UPDATE
E3-S2 AC4: doctor-active check is part of the conditional UPDATE (or joined in it), not only a prior lookup
E3-S2 AC5: POST /api/appointments guarded by require_roles(PATIENT); doctor and admin 403, no token 401

E3-S2 AC6: PaymentService obtained via the overridable dependency in api/deps.py, charge called once after the booking transaction commits; fee serialised as a 2-decimal string through types/money.py (never float)
Layering: router -> booking_service -> repositories; no SQL in the router; appointment fee is a snapshot taken from the doctor profile at booking time
